clue.text: Assuming quiet service-men drink sitting

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
RE, the Royal Engineers, are British army servicemen
to sup is to drink
posing, as for a portrait, is sitting

explanation.surface: Someone takes it for granted that quiet soldiers will drink sitting down.
explanation.definitionFit: Presupposing something means taking it for granted beforehand, just as assuming does.

clue.text: The way coppers like a man who is wise

parts.note: p, pence, are copper coins in British money
as means like
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Police resemble a wise man in how they go about things.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a way through, a corridor or route.

clue.text: Sound exercise for certain animals

indicators.note: Sound says the word for exercise is heard rather than written

parts.note: to use is to exercise, as a right

explanation.surface: Healthy exercise is recommended for some animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewes are female sheep, a particular kind of animal.

clue.text: Scare, and maybe even run

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters of even run can be put in another order

explanation.surface: Something might frighten you, and perhaps even make you run.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve is to rattle someone's courage, to frighten.

clue.text: Display will be made by attend, ant social worker

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
the ant is a social insect, and a worker ant does the labour

explanation.surface: A show is staged by a helper and a welfare officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a grand public show or spectacle.

clue.text: Mark tops up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word tops is written from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A grade is raised to the very best.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a mark or stain.

clue.text: It's an arrangement the queen finds less attractive

indicators.note: an arrangement sets the letters of its an in a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, denotes the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch finds a particular floral arrangement rather ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' reorders ITSAN into NASTI, then ER is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning more unpleasant or ugly.

clue.text: There's great apprehension about the importance for a boxer

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the next

parts.note: fear is great apprehension
weight means importance or significance

explanation.surface: Everyone is anxious about how much a fighter's role matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A featherweight is a boxer in a light weight class.

clue.text: The churchman in the solicitor's office?

definitions.text: The churchman in the solicitor's office?

parts.words: The churchman in the solicitor's office?
parts.note: clerk once meant a cleric; here it is a trainee bound by contract to a solicitor

explanation.surface: A clergyman is found working in a law firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An articled clerk was a trainee solicitor bound by articles; clerk originally meant clergyman.

clue.text: Oriental variety of sea-gull

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of sea are given a new order

parts.note: a tern is a gull-like seabird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots an exotic Eastern kind of sea-gull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges SEA into EAS; the tern then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things from the East, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: He'll make complaint right after the game

indicators.note: right comes after the game, so its letter is placed following it

parts.note: grouse is a game bird shot for sport

explanation.surface: A shooter grumbles straight after the day's game shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouser is a grumbler, someone who habitually makes complaint.

clue.text: Gin has some backing

indicators.note: backing means the word for some is read from back to front

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: A bottle of gin gets partial financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the drink but is the snare used for catching game.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for animals, so it is a device for catching prey.

clue.text: A bishop with an island off the Scottish coast

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop travels with a companion to a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: The woman who's married one twice

indicators.note: twice says the pair of letters is written two times over

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman has been married once, then a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: MIMI is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Boheme, a familiar crossword woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is a female first name, so it stands for a particular woman.

clue.text: He sculpted the little river god

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
Odin is the chief Norse god

explanation.surface: An artist carved a small statue of a river deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker.

clue.text: Open a Continental drinking place

parts.note: un is French for a
a bar is a place to drink

explanation.surface: Someone opens a cafe-bar in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbar a door is to remove its bar, opening it.

clue.text: Notices foreign money gives offence to the viewer

parts.note: eyes as a verb means looks at or notices
the ore is a coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Someone spots foreign cash and finds it offends the onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly sight, something that offends whoever looks at it.

clue.text: Some rotten drilling-rig guy little twister

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A decaying oil rig is held by a guy-rope that twists a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant's tendril coils round supports, acting as a small twisting guy-rope.

clue.text: To take flight carrying sound equipment can be tiring

indicators.note: carrying means one word holds the other within it

parts.note: to wing is to fly, to take flight
the ear is the body's equipment for sound

explanation.surface: Flying while lugging audio gear can wear a traveller out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearing is exhausting, a synonym of tiring.

clue.text: The musician's full of life

parts.note: the clue reads as a lively player, but it means a performer's term for lively playing

explanation.surface: A performer has enormous energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Animato is an Italian score direction meaning play in an animated, lively way.

clue.text: Possibly offering to forgo a point-the dog!

indicators.note: possibly says the remaining letters may be shuffled into a new order
to forgo is to do without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: An offering may be refused at a point, says an exasperated dog owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to forgo' drops E from OFFERING, leaving OFFRING, and 'Possibly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The griffon is a breed of wiry-coated dog.

clue.text: Slander perhaps seemed most unpleasant

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of slander could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Defamatory talk seemed thoroughly nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who snarled growled angrily, behaving and looking at their nastiest.

clue.text: The boards divided about alter native accommodation

indicators.note: the boards are split apart and placed around the next word

parts.note: the boards is the theatre stage
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Theatre floorboards are split up to make room for something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is space for keeping things, a sort of accommodation for goods.

clue.text: One may well do this, if lacking sound sense

definitions.text: One may well do this, if lacking sound sense

parts.words: One may well do this, if lacking sound sense
parts.note: sound sense means the sense of hearing; someone without it watches lips instead

explanation.surface: A person without good judgement might take this course.
explanation.definitionFit: Deaf people often follow speech by watching the speaker's mouth movements.

clue.text: Her make-up is in rainbow colours!

definitions.text: Her make-up is in rainbow colours!

parts.words: Her make-up is in rainbow colours!
parts.note: the rainbow goddess of Greek myth, and also the coloured part of the eye or a many-hued flower

explanation.surface: A woman wears garishly bright cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek messenger goddess personified the rainbow, and the eye's coloured ring shares her name.

clue.text: The guide having to edge back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled run is read in reverse

parts.note: a lip is an edge, as of a cup

explanation.surface: A tour guide has to step back from a cliff edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot steers ships through difficult waters, a guide by profession.

clue.text: Work with a pupil making stone

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
L, learner, as on a learner driver's plate, is a pupil

explanation.surface: A craftsman works with an apprentice to make a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone, so it is a precious stone.

clue.text: A poet is given nothing in a carrier

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hod is a builder's carrier for bricks
O, the round figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A versifier is handed nothing inside a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hood was a 19th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hood wrote The Song of the Shirt, so the surname names a poet.

clue.text: Lake and country

explanation.surface: A list of places mentions a lake and a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A land is a nation or region, so it means country.

clue.text: Prevent the carrying out of capital punishment?

definitions.text: the carrying out of capital punishment?

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: To head off is to forestall something; literally, beheading is cutting the top off a person.

clue.text: The non-professional gives a dull turn to deplore

parts.note: mat, or matt, means dull, not glossy

indicators.note: turn means the word for deplore is turned to read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret or deplore

explanation.surface: An unpaid performer gives a lacklustre act that is lamentable.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part for love rather than pay, unlike a professional.

clue.text: A deed done-how stupid-how stupid!

indicators.note: stupid suggests a senseless jumble of the letters before it

explanation.surface: An exasperated onlooker reacts to a foolish action twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodenheaded means dull-witted, as though with a block of wood for a head.
